name: GM LS3 6.2 L V8 (Corvette C6, 2008-2013)
summary: Cross-plane pushrod V8: even 90-degree firing overall but uneven pulses within each bank (180-270-180-90), which through per-bank manifolds gives the classic American V8 burble.

rod_length_mm.note: 6.098 in, powdered metal I-beam. Vendor tech guide, not a GM document.

firing_order.note: Numbering (chevygeek.com): odd cylinders 1-3-5-7 on the driver (left) side front to rear, even 2-4-6-8 on the passenger (right) side, cylinder 1 at the front.

crank.value: cross-plane: four throws at 90 degrees, each pin shared by one cylinder from each bank
crank.note: Wikipedia's Crossplane article describes the general layout; the LS page does not use the word. Standard for this engine family.

firing_intervals_deg.note: Even 90 degrees engine-wide. PER BANK it is uneven: left bank (1,3,5,7) fires 1, then 7 after 180, 5 after 270, 3 after 180, back to 1 after 90; right bank (8,2,6,4) fires 8, 2 after 180, 6 after 90, 4 after 180, 8 after 270. Those per-bank figures are my own calculation from the firing order and numbering; they match Wikipedia's general statement that crossplane V8 banks fire at 180-90-180-270.

exhaust_lift_mm.note: 0.525 in. A search-result summary of Chevrolet's crate-engine listing showed .522 in (page not opened).

lobe_separation_deg.note: No variable valve timing on the LS3. Individual opening/closing events not published on the pages opened.

redline_rpm.note: Wikipedia: large valves limit maximum rpm to 6600 in the LS3. Corvette Action Center article also refers to the 6600 rpm rev limiter.

peak_power_kw.note: 430 bhp SAE certified at 5,900 rpm, standard exhaust; converted by me. 436 hp with the optional dual-mode exhaust.

peak_torque_nm.note: 424 lb-ft at 4,600 rpm; 428 lb-ft with dual-mode exhaust.

intake_type.value: plenum ('car-style' intake manifold) with a single 90 mm electronic throttle body

intake_port_volume_cc.note: Rectangular intake port, cylinder head casting 821.

header_type.note: Not documented on an opened page (production cars use one cast manifold per bank, but that is from memory, not a source).

exhaust_pipe_dia_mm.note: Stated for the optional dual-mode exhaust (2.5 in), compared with 3 in on the Z06.

sources.what: PSI Conversion LS3 swap guide. Vendor-compiled spec table (block, rotating assembly, heads, cam). Not GM, but detailed and consistent with GM crate-engine figures.
Wikipedia, GM LS-based small-block engine. Bore, displacement, CR, valve sizes, power, rev limit, firing order.
chevygeek.com LS firing order page (cited by Wikipedia). Cylinder numbering by bank.
Wikipedia, Crossplane. Per-bank interval pattern of cross-plane V8s.
Corvette Action Center technical article on the 2008 LS3 with GM engineer interviews. Rev limiter, valvetrain background.

vehicle.name: Chevrolet Corvette coupe (C6, 2008, six-speed manual)

curb_kg.note: 'Weight: ... 3,217 lbs / 1,459 kg (Coupe)'. CorvSport's 2008 page gives 'Curb Weight 3,179 lbs.' for the coupe (https://www.corvsport.com/2008-corvette-specifications/); CorvSport's same page lists the 2005-era 4L65-E four-speed automatic for 2008, which is wrong for that year, so Corvette: Year by Year is preferred (my judgement).

gear_count.note: 'Hydra-Matic 2006 6L80 (MYC) Six Speed'. Options table: 'MX0 Six-speed Paddle Shift Automatic Transmission (coupe and convertible) 19,136 (54.19%) $1,250.00', so the automatic was an option but the most common gearbox (the Z06, manual only, is included in the percentage base).

gears.note: 'Manual Six Speed Transmission: 1st Gear 2.66:1, 2nd 1.78:1, 3rd 1.30:1, 4th 1.00:1, 5th .74:1, 6th .50:1 ... Final Drive Ratio 3.42'; Tremec TR6060 (MM6): 2.664/1.783/1.302/1.000/0.741/0.502 on https://corvetteactioncenter.com/specs/c6/2008/2008tr6060.html; CorvSport agrees (https://www.corvsport.com/2008-corvette-specifications/). Chosen over the automatic (see alternative_automatic) because the simulator models a clutch.

wheel_radius_m.note: Calculated by me from the tyre size (half the rim diameter plus section width times aspect ratio): the unloaded geometric radius, not a published rolling radius; the loaded rolling radius is a few percent smaller.

tyre.note: 'Tire Size: P245/40ZR-18 (Front) P285/35ZR-19 (Rear) (Goodyear Eagle F1 GS, Extended Mobility)'. Rear-wheel drive. CorvSport gives the same rear size.

top_speed_kmh.note: Not found for the 2008 automatic coupe in the sources read.

driven.note: English Wikipedia, 'Chevrolet Corvette (C6)' (read 2026-11-17), infobox layout: Front mid-engine, rear-wheel-drive.

missing: a GM document for the 2008 curb weight and 6L80 ratios (two enthusiast references read)

sources.what: Corvette: Year by Year (corvettestory.com) 2008 specifications and options page: transmission ratios, axle ratios, tyre sizes, weights, option production counts.
CorvSport 2008 Corvette specifications: manual gear ratios, tyres, coupe curb weight. Its automatic entry is wrong for 2008.

alternative_automatic.note: The six-speed 6L80 automatic (option MX0), 54.19% of 2008 Corvettes, as researched by the data pass; not modelled because the simulator has a clutch, not a torque converter.

gears.note: '1st Gear 4.03:1, 2nd Gear 2.36:1, 3rd Gear 1.53:1, 4th Gear 1.15:1, 5th Gear 0.85:1, 6th Gear 0.67:1, Reverse Gear 3.06:1'. Manual (standard) for reference: 'Manual Six Speed Transmission: 1st Gear 2.66:1, 2nd 1.78:1, 3rd 1.30:1, 4th 1.00:1, 5th .74:1, 6th .50:1 ... Final Drive Ratio 3.42'; CorvSport agrees for the manual (https://www.corvsport.com/2008-corvette-specifications/).

final_drive.note: 6L80 entry: 'Final Drive Ratio 2.56'. Options: 'GU2 Real [sic] Axle 2.73 Ratio (with automatic transmission) 8,839 (25.03%)', so 2.56 was standard and still the commoner axle with the automatic (19,136 automatics, 8,839 with GU2; the subtraction is mine).
